title: Module Re-exports Advanced
story: Your networking library has deeply nested internals: `net.protocol.tcp.socket.connect()`. That's a nightmare for users. Advanced re-exports let you present a clean API while keeping your internals perfectly organized.
why: Advanced re-export patterns including glob re-exports and selective re-exports give you complete control over your module's public API surface.
analogy: A luxury hotel has a massive service basement: kitchens, laundry, maintenance, storage — all meticulously organized. But guests only see the lobby, elevators, and their room. Re-exports are the lobby: a curated, simple interface to complex internals.
try_it: Create an `app` module with three internal submodules: `auth`, `data`, `ui`. Each has 2-3 functions. Use re-exports to create a public API with only 5 functions total, hiding implementation details and renaming where needed for clarity.
tips: Hide internal modules entirely if users don't need direct access
Use `as` for renaming: `pub use internal::fn as public_name;`
The internal module can stay `mod` (private) — only the re-export needs `pub`
common_mistakes: Re-exporting everything — defeats the purpose of encapsulation
Creating confusing rename paths — keep re-exported names intuitive
Forgetting to mark internal items as `pub` — re-exports can't expose private items
